paper_metadata.title: Effects of Cu additions on microstructures and mechanical properties of Al0.1CoCrFeNiCux high-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: The effects of Cu additions on microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of Al0.1CoCrFeNiCux (x = 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5) high entropy alloys (HEA) prepared via the arc melting technique over a wide temperature range are investigated.
For Al0.1CoCrFeNiCu𝑥 alloys before tension loading, the intensity of the {200} peak gradually in-creases as the Cu content increases.

All alloys are fabricated by arc melting in a high-purity argon atmosphere. High-purity (99.9 wt%) raw elements are weighed according to the nominal molar ratios and thoroughly mixed. The alloys are melted at 1950 K, and each ingot are remelted five times to ensure complete melting and homogeneity. After melting, the ingots are cast into water-cooled copper molds to form cylindrical alloys with dimensions of 30 mm and 100 mm in length.
